description:
Eight of env's sixteen keys (out, nest, live, live_names, stmt, guard, loop, depth; `scope/1` compiler.ex ~L1352) are the copy analysis's liveness scope, rebuilt by hand at five sites with slightly different rules: `scope/1`, `nested/2`, `loop_env/2`, the inline env (`inline`, calls section) and `acc_env`. `Defk.Copies` today is 30 pure AST queries with no state; the transitions live in the compiler. Deletion test: deleting Copies moves 30 functions; the complexity is in the transitions.

Settled shape (grilling 2026-10-19):
- `Defk.Copies` grows to own the scope, as `Defk.Strip` owns record and classifier. Transitions: `enter_stmt/2`, `leave_block/2`, `nested_arm/2`, `loop/2`, `inline_call/3`; one question `must_copy?/2`. The 30 queries become its implementation (private where nothing else calls them).
- env carries the scope under one key, `:scope`. The sequential state (writes log, alias classes) stays at `ctx.lowering.copies`; two homes for state, one module for the rules.
- `before_write/3`, `hoist/3`, `range_dest`, alloc zeroing and range copies ask the scope instead of reading env keys.
- CONTEXT.md: sharpen the "Copy analysis" entry to name its scope (no new term).
- docs/agents/compiler-map.md: the "array values" row and the Copies bullet.

Tests: a unit test for `must_copy?` and the transitions (no C); value_semantics_test keeps counting `defk_copy_` as the end-to-end check, or reads the `:copy` report topic.

Gate: byte-identical `mix dump_c`; `mix ci`; PR per AGENTS.md.

comments.text: PR #58: Defk.Copies.Scope at env.scope; C unchanged; mix ci green (2294 passed).

title: Defk.Copies owns the copy analysis's liveness scope (eight env keys become one)
